project.name: ComplexAnalysis
project.description: Complex Fréchet differentiability on open subsets of finite-dimensional complex normed spaces implies local analyticity for maps into complete complex normed spaces. The proof uses an iterated polydisc Cauchy formula, analytic continuous-function-valued kernels, and bounded vector-valued integration. The integration API is independently importable.

sources.title: The classical Cauchy integral formula on polydiscs

headlines.title: Finite-dimensional differentiability implies analyticity
headlines.text:
([`DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd_of_finiteDimensional`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/complex-analysis/blob/c22c803e257c294edf0528a584b66e2735316717/ComplexAnalysis/Analysis/Complex/FiniteDimensional.lean)).
A complex Fréchet-differentiable map on an open subset of a finite-dimensional
complex normed space is analytic near every point of that set, when its target
is a complete complex normed space; dimension zero is included.

headlines.title: Differentiability–analyticity equivalence
headlines.text:
([`analyticOnNhd_iff_differentiableOn_of_finiteDimensional`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/complex-analysis/blob/c22c803e257c294edf0528a584b66e2735316717/ComplexAnalysis/Analysis/Complex/FiniteDimensional.lean)).
On such an open set, analyticity near every point is equivalent to complex
Fréchet differentiability, under the same source and target hypotheses.

headlines.title: Polydisc Cauchy formula
headlines.text:
([`DifferentiableOn.torusIntegral_cauchy`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/complex-analysis/blob/c22c803e257c294edf0528a584b66e2735316717/ComplexAnalysis/Analysis/Complex/TorusCauchy.lean)).
A complex-differentiable map on a positive-radius closed coordinate polydisc,
valued in a complete complex normed space, agrees at interior points with
its normalized torus boundary integral.

headlines.title: Polynomial boundary degree counts interior roots
headlines.text:
([`Polynomial.degree_normalizedCircleMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/complex-analysis/blob/c22c803e257c294edf0528a584b66e2735316717/ComplexAnalysis/Analysis/Complex/PolynomialBoundary.lean)).
A complex polynomial with no zeros on the unit circle gives an unbased continuous
circle self-map by normalizing its values. Its degree equals the number of roots
strictly inside the unit disk, counted with multiset multiplicity. Nonmonic
polynomials, repeated roots and nonzero constants of arbitrary phase are included.

headlines.title: Exterior polynomial root-scaling homotopy
headlines.text:
([`Polynomial.normalizedCircleMapScaleRootsHomotopy`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/complex-analysis/blob/c22c803e257c294edf0528a584b66e2735316717/ComplexAnalysis/Analysis/Complex/PolynomialExterior.lean)).
If `p.eval w ≠ 0` whenever `1 ≤ ‖w‖`, root scaling over the real unit interval
joins the normalized leading monomial to the canonical normalized boundary map.
Its characteristic value is `normalize ((p.scaleRoots (t : ℂ)).eval z)`.
The leading coefficient's arbitrary phase is retained; the corresponding degree
statement is `Circle.degree (p.normalizedCircleMap _) = (p.natDegree : ℤ)`.

headlines.title: Compact scalar-kernel operators
headlines.text:
([`ContinuousMap.kernelOperator`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/complex-analysis/blob/c22c803e257c294edf0528a584b66e2735316717/ComplexAnalysis/MeasureTheory/Integral/Kernel.lean)).
A continuous scalar kernel on `X × Y`, with compact `Y` and a finite Borel
measure, gives a compact complex-linear map from `L²(Y, μ)` to `C(X, ℂ)`.
The parameter space `X` is arbitrary; compactness of `X` is needed only for
the sup-norm bound. The construction uses a generic transpose of an
operator-norm-continuous field, compact whenever its normed target is proper.

headlines.title: Detecting finite eigenspaces of compact positive squares
headlines.text:
([`ContinuousLinearMap.exists_eigenvector_comp_adjoint_detected`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/complex-analysis/blob/c22c803e257c294edf0528a584b66e2735316717/ComplexAnalysis/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/CompactOperator.lean)).
On an arbitrary complete real or complex Hilbert space, compact `T` and
continuous linear `B` with `B.comp T ≠ 0` give a nonzero eigenvalue of
`T.comp T.adjoint` whose finite-dimensional eigenspace contains a vector
`v` with `B v ≠ 0`. No separability or commutation hypothesis is needed.
